task_instance: Load a small CSV (>100K rows) with cudf.read_csv, run a groupby/sum and a merge (mirroring pandas), and verify results match pandas (Path 2: Explicit cuDF API from the skill).
blocker_detail: cuDF requires an NVIDIA GPU (Volta+ on CUDA 12, or Turing+ on CUDA 13) with a working CUDA driver to execute any DataFrame operation on the GPU. This container has no GPU device: `nvidia-smi` is not installed, there is no /dev/nvidia* device node, `lspci` shows no NVIDIA hardware, and there is no CUDA driver library present (libcuda.so.1 not found anywhere on the filesystem, dlopen fails with 'cannot open shared object file'). The cudf-cu12 wheel itself is resolvable/downloadable via pip in this sandbox (metadata fetch succeeded), but installing the Python package cannot substitute for the missing GPU hardware/driver — any cudf import or operation would fail at the CUDA runtime level (no CUDA-capable device found), not due to a missing pip package. This is a hardware capability the runtime does not grant, not something installable.
evidence: Ran `nvidia-smi` -> command not found. `ls /dev/nvidia*` -> No such file or directory. `lspci | grep -i nvidia` -> no output (no NVIDIA hardware). `python3 -c "import cudf"` -> ModuleNotFoundError (not installed). `pip3 install --dry-run cudf-cu12` -> successfully resolved and began listing cudf-cu12 26.8.1 and its CUDA-toolkit/cupy/numba-cuda dependencies (shows package retrieval itself is not the blocker). `find / -iname libcuda.so*` -> no results. `python3 -c "import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1')"` -> OSError: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory. Concluded the skill's core deliverable (running actual cuDF GPU DataFrame operations, per Path 1/2/3 in the SKILL.md) cannot be attempted or verified in this runtime because there is no GPU/CUDA driver at all, and stopped rather than working around it (no attempt to fake/mock GPU execution).
